inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: This looks less like a genuine path to peace and more like a coordinated attempt to dictate terms to Iran while keeping the threat of force in reserve. The US sent its 15-point plan through Pakistan, but Iran’s five counter-conditions—including an end to aggression, compensation, and recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz—show that the underlying dispute is being papered over, not resolved. Israel’s insistence on a right to pre-emptive strikes makes the real priority plain: preserve the option to escalate while presenting diplomacy as cover. Don’t mistake a proposal for proof that those driving the conflict intend to end it.
